summary.text: Shale is a fine-grained clastic sedimentary rock formed from mud made of clay mineral flakes and tiny silt-sized bits of other minerals, especially quartz and calcite.
Its clay flakes lie parallel, so it tends to split into thin layers less than a centimeter thick, a property called fissility.
Shale is the most common sedimentary rock, and it is usually laid down in very slow-moving water where its fine particles can finally settle.

facts.label: Organic matter
facts.value: Mudrocks hold about 95% of sedimentary rocks' organic matter

facts.label: Layer thickness
facts.value: Splits into layers under one centimeter thick

items.prompt: A muddy river flows into a calm lake. Where do the finest clay and silt particles end up?

options.label: Settled in still water, long after the sand
Dropped first, right at the river mouth
Floating on the surface for good
Dissolved completely into the lake

items.explain: Fine particles stay suspended long after sand has dropped out, so shale is typically deposited in very slow-moving water such as lakes.

items.prompt: Single clay particles sink extremely slowly. What happens when muddy river water meets salty seawater?

options.label: The clay dissolves in the salt water
The clay rises and floats on top
The clay quickly clumps into larger clusters
The clay turns into grains of sand

items.explain: Flocculation is very rapid in highly saline seawater, turning particles under 4 microns into clumps tens to hundreds of microns across.

items.prompt: Why does shale tend to split into thin, flat sheets when you strike it?

options.label: Water freezes and expands between its grains
Its clay mineral flakes are lined up parallel
It is built of many glued quartz crystals
Its grains were melted and then recooled

items.explain: The parallel orientation of the clay mineral flakes makes shale break into thin layers along its bedding.

items.prompt: A cliff shows red shale in one layer and green shale just above it. What change most likely explains the shift in color?

options.label: The green layer formed with more oxygen around
The green layer is rich in copper
The red layer was baked by lava
Its iron went from oxidized to reduced

items.explain: Shale shifts from reddish to greenish as iron in the oxidized (ferric) state is converted to the reduced (ferrous) state.

items.prompt: A thick band of black shale is found in a cliff. What does it suggest about the water where its mud settled?

options.label: It was warm, clear and fast-moving
It was low in oxygen
It was frozen over for years
It was rich in dissolved iron rust

items.explain: Black shale contains over one percent carbonaceous material and points to a reducing setting; black shales form in anoxic conditions.

items.prompt: Shale can let water pass through it while holding back dissolved salts, and most shales formed in the sea. What is groundwater trapped in shale often like?

options.label: Pure, fresh drinking water
Mostly oil instead of water
Highly salty
Boiling hot and acidic

items.explain: Most shales are marine, and groundwater in shale formations is often highly saline; shale may act as a semipermeable layer that keeps salts in.
